intro: I study machine learning from the vantage point of pure mathematics — asking which analytic, geometric, and topological structures make learning possible, and how those structures translate into models that generate, infer, and reason. Six threads organize the work.

areas.title: Generative Models
areas.summary: Learning to sample from complex, high-dimensional distributions — from denoising diffusion and implicit samplers to autoregressive and latent-variable models.
areas.detail: How do we turn noise into structure? I work across the modern generative landscape: score-based diffusion, deterministic samplers, normalizing flows, adversarial and energy-based models, and variational autoencoders — with a bias toward the underlying probabilistic and dynamical principles rather than architecture alone.

areas.title: Stochastic Processes & SDEs
areas.summary: Reading generative modeling through stochastic calculus: diffusion as a stochastic differential equation, and the search for processes better suited to data.
areas.detail: The score-based view recasts generation as integrating a reverse-time SDE. I am interested in which stochastic processes — beyond the standard Brownian scaffold — are analytically and topologically better matched to real data, particularly structured and time-series data.

areas.title: Density Estimation & Inference
areas.summary: Estimating and approximating distributions — variational inference, expectation–maximization, and exact-likelihood models.
areas.detail: From mean-field and automatic-differentiation variational inference to the EM algorithm and change-of-variables likelihoods, I study how we quantify uncertainty and fit densities to data, and where these approximations succeed or break down.

areas.title: Topological & Geometric ML
areas.summary: Bringing topology and geometry to bear on learning: persistent homology, manifold structure, and homeomorphism interpolation via Neural ODEs.
areas.detail: Data has shape. I use tools from algebraic topology — persistent homology and beyond — to characterize that shape, and study continuous-depth models (Neural ODEs) as homeomorphisms that deform latent space while preserving topological invariants.

areas.title: Graph Neural Networks
areas.summary: Learning on relational structure — spectral convolution and attention over graphs.
areas.detail: Much of the world is relational. I study message passing, graph convolution, and graph attention as principled ways to learn representations on non-Euclidean domains, and how spectral and geometric perspectives illuminate their behavior.

areas.title: Mathematical Foundations of Deep Learning
areas.summary: The through-line: differential equations, stochastic calculus, and topology as the grammar behind deep models.
areas.detail: Across all of the above sits one conviction — that abstract mathematics is a generative source of ideas for learning, not just an after-the-fact justification. Flows and differential equations, diffusion and stochastic calculus, latent spaces and topology: I want to keep pulling these threads.
